Hi all —

Thanks for the draft, Rachel. I made edits and simplified some of the legal shorthand so procurement gets exactly what they need. Key recommendations:

1) Executive summary (paste-ready):
- "Redwood Inference processes customer content to provide hosted inference. For customers in jurisdictions that restrict cross-border transfers, we support Data Residency configuration where requests may be routed to regional infrastructure. For transfers outside the customer-specified region, we rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for adequacy and maintain technical and organizational safeguards (encryption in transit and at rest, strict access controls, and subprocessors limited to cloud and infra partners)."

2) FAQ (3 short Qs) — examples to include:
- Q: Do you transfer customer data outside of the EU/UK?
  A: We only transfer data as needed for processing and for customers who choose global hosting; transfers are governed by our DPA and SCCs.
- Q: Where can I find the subprocessors list?
  A: We publish an up-to-date subprocessors map: https://app.redwood.com/docs/subprocessors-map and include this in the DPA appendix.
- Q: What encryption and safeguards do you use?
  A: All customer content is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3+) and at rest. We apply role-based access, key management integrations (KMS/HSM), and logging/audit trails.

3) Console microcopy (Data Residency toggle, single line):
- "Data residency: choose a region. Cross-border transfers occur only as described in our DPA (SCCs and additional safeguards)."

4) Procurement asks to include a link to the DPA appendix and a short note about subprocessors cadence (we update quarterly).

I attached a revised explainer (v0.2) and a one-page FAQ you can hand to procurement. Vivek — please flag any required legal additions (SCC references, BAA nuances for healthcare customers).

Laura Bennett
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Thanks — good, concise work. A couple of legal clarifications to add before we hand to procurement:

- SCCs: call them out as "EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs)" on the FAQ and link to the published SCC text.
- Supplementary measures: include a short parenthetical that we implement additional technical and organizational measures to provide a similar level of protection when transfers rely on SCCs.
- Healthcare (important): for U.S. HIPAA-covered entities we can sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted (multi-tenant) customers, we offer contracts with standard DPA controls but BAAs may require a dedicated environment and additional operational attestations. Please do not promise a BAA for hosted until we confirm the deployment type.
- Subprocessors cadence: Quarterly updates; include timestamp of last update in the PDF.

Suggested one-line console microcopy (shorter):
"Data residency: select a region — transfers are handled under our DPA and EU SCCs; see details."

I'll add a short legal paragraph for the DPA appendix and link to the subprocessors map. Rachel — if you want, I can join your procurement call to cover the BAA/deployment nuance.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
